formatNotes: First Games held in Madison, Wisconsin (and first outside California since 2009) after the move from the StubHub Center. 40 men and 40 women qualified through the Open and Regionals; the official leaderboard lists 39 men (including Ricky Garard, later DQ'd, and Mitchell Sinnamon, WD) and 40 women (Carleen Mathews DNF, Camille Leblanc-Bazinet and Chelsey Hughes WD). No cuts were made during the weekend; all athletes contested all 13 events. Every event was worth up to 100 points to the winner on CrossFit's graduated points table. Minimum work requirements were introduced for Run Swim Run and the Sprint O-Course. After the Games, third-place finisher Ricky Garard tested positive for testolone and endurobol, was disqualified and banned for four years; Patrick Vellner was elevated to third. The official leaderboard still displays Garard's event scores (including two event wins) with a DQ overall.
yearSummary: The 2017 Games opened the Madison era with the widest mix of disciplines the sport had seen: a lake swim-run, a cyclocross bike race, a head-to-head obstacle course, a strongman medley and a sledgehammer 'banger', alongside classic tests like a 1RM snatch, an extended Amanda, and a heavy Open rework. Mathew Fraser won four events (Triple-G Chipper, Muscle-Up Clean Ladder, Heavy 17.5, 2223 Intervals) and repeated as champion with a record 216-point margin over Brent Fikowski. The women's race was the closest in Games history at the time: Tia-Clair Toomey, runner-up the two previous years, edged fellow Australian Kara Webb by 2 points after Webb beat her by 0.19 seconds in the Fibonacci Final. The year is also remembered for the first doping disqualification of a podium finisher, Ricky Garard, who was stripped of third place.

events.name: Run Swim Run
events.description:
For time:
Run 1.5 miles
Swim 500 meters
Run 1.5 miles

Athletes start at the Alliant Energy Center, run 1.5 miles to Lake Monona, swim 500 meters around a series of buoys, then return along the same 1.5-mile run course to the finish.
events.notes: Offsite opener and the first freshwater (lake) swim in Games history, in Lake Monona. One of the events where a minimum work requirement was introduced this year. The men's and women's winning times were nearly identical (28:45.29 vs 28:45.65).

events.name: Cyclocross
events.description:
3 laps of a purpose-built cyclocross course for time.

On Wednesday, August 2, each athlete rode the course as an individual time trial; the time trial was used only to seed the heats. On Thursday the field raced the course in two 20-athlete heats, 3 laps each, on a technical off-road circuit built on the Alliant Energy Center grounds with climbs, descents and obstacles that could force dismounts.
events.notes: First dedicated bicycle race in Games history (bikes had previously appeared only in the 2012 Camp Pendleton triathlon). Source conflict on the men's winner: the official leaderboard still shows Ricky Garard first at 19:26.72 (his overall result is marked DQ after his doping ban), while Wikipedia credits Mathew Fraser (2nd across the line, 19:52.68) as the winner following Garard's disqualification.

events.name: Amanda .45
events.description:
13-11-9-7-5 reps for time of:
Ring muscle-ups
Squat snatches (135 lb men / 95 lb women)

Time cap: 13 minutes for men, 15 minutes for women.
events.notes: Thursday night in the Coliseum. An extended version of the benchmark Amanda (9-7-5 muscle-ups and squat snatches, contested at the 2010 Games), adding 13- and 11-rep rounds. The time cap differed by division: 13 minutes for men, 15 for women.

events.name: Sprint O-Course
events.description:
Head-to-head sprint through a purpose-built obstacle course, run as a three-round bracketed tournament.

Round 1: 8 heats of 5 athletes; the top 2 in each heat advance, plus the 4 fastest non-qualifiers (20 athletes to round 2).
Round 2: 4 heats of 5; each heat winner advances plus the fastest non-winner (5 athletes to the final).
Final: 5 athletes race for places 1-5.
Athletes eliminated in round 2 take places 6-20 and those eliminated in round 1 take places 21-40, ranked by their round times.
events.notes: First obstacle-course event since the 2012 Camp Pendleton O-course, this time on a purpose-built course on the Alliant Energy Center grounds. Scored by tournament placement rather than a single time (leaderboard shows placement points). One of the events where a minimum work requirement was introduced.

events.name: 1RM Snatch
events.description:
1-rep-max snatch.

One athlete lifts at a time, with a lift taking place every 20 seconds. Each athlete gets 2 attempts; the 10 athletes with the heaviest successful lifts then get 2 additional attempts in a final round. Score is the heaviest successful snatch.
events.notes: Contested in the Coliseum. Garret Fisher's 305-lb snatch was the heaviest snatch ever at the CrossFit Games at the time. Kara Webb (now Kara Saunders) won the women's event at 203 lb.

events.name: Triple-G Chipper
events.description:
For time:
100 pull-ups
80 GHD sit-ups
60 one-legged squats (pistols), alternating
40-cal. row
20 dumbbell push presses (single dumbbell, 100 lb men / 70 lb women)

Time cap: 15 minutes.
events.notes: Friday night in the Coliseum. The push presses used one very heavy dumbbell (100/70 lb). First of Fraser's four event wins.

events.name: Assault Banger
events.description:
For time:
40-cal. Assault bike (men) / 30-cal. Assault bike (women)
20-ft. Banger

After finishing the calories on the Assault bike, athletes use a sledgehammer to drive a weighted 'banger' sled 20 feet down a track to the finish.

Time cap: 6 minutes.
events.notes: Debut of the 'banger': a sled in a track that athletes advance by striking it with a sledgehammer. Calorie requirement differed by division (40 men / 30 women).

events.name: Strongman's Fear
events.description:
For time, move a yoke, a pair of farmers logs, and a sled from one end of the field to the other in two 60-ft. stages:
60-ft. yoke carry, then 60-ft. handstand walk
60-ft. farmers log carry, then 60-ft. handstand walk
60-ft. sled drag
Repeat the sequence to bring all three implements from midfield to the finish (120 ft. total per implement).

Athletes may move the implements in any order, but must handstand walk 60 ft. back each time they return to retrieve the next implement.

Loads: 500-lb yoke, 200-lb farmers logs (each), 400-lb sled for men; 340-lb yoke, 120-lb farmers logs (each), 310-lb sled for women.

Time cap: 10 minutes.
events.notes: Contested outdoors on the North Park field. The event returned at the 2018 and 2019 Games, making it a recurring test.

events.name: Muscle-Up Clean Ladder
events.description:
8 rounds for time of:
4 bar muscle-ups
2 cleans, ascending in load each round

Men's clean loads: 225, 245, 265, 285, 305, 320, 335, 350 lb.
Women's clean loads: 145, 160, 175, 190, 205, 215, 225, 235 lb.

Time cap: 11 minutes. Athletes who do not finish are scored by reps completed, with a tiebreak based on the time of their last successful rep.
events.notes: Saturday night in the Coliseum. The final bars (350/235 lb) approached 1RM territory for much of the field after 32 bar muscle-ups.

events.name: Heavy 17.5
events.description:
10 rounds for time of:
9 thrusters (125 lb men / 85 lb women)
35 double-unders

Time cap: 12 minutes.
events.notes: A heavier version of Open workout 17.5, which used 95/65-lb thrusters with the same 10 rounds of 9 thrusters and 35 double-unders.

events.name: Madison Triplet
events.description:
5 rounds for time of:
Run 450 meters
7 hay bale clean burpees (100-lb sandbag men / 70-lb sandbag women)

For each hay bale clean burpee, the athlete lifts the sandbag from the ground, throws it over the hay bale wall, drops chest-to-ground in a burpee, then jumps over the hay bale wall to the other side.

Time cap: 20 minutes.
events.notes: Sunday morning outdoors in North Park, a nod to Wisconsin farm country with the hay bale walls. Source conflict on the men's winner: the official leaderboard still shows Ricky Garard first at 15:48.92 (overall DQ for doping), while Wikipedia credits Patrick Vellner (2nd across the line, 16:29.58) as the winner following Garard's disqualification.

events.name: 2223 Intervals
events.description:
Working in intervals of 2:00, 2:00, 2:00, then 3:00, with 1 minute of rest between intervals, complete 75 overhead squats.

Each interval begins with:
2 rope climbs
10-cal. SkiErg (men) / 7-cal. SkiErg (women)
then max-rep overhead squats (155 lb men / 105 lb women) in the time remaining.

The event ends when the athlete completes 75 total overhead squats or at the end of the final 3-minute interval (12 minutes total elapsed). Scored by time of the 75th overhead squat; athletes who do not finish are scored by reps.
events.notes: The event name comes from the interval structure: 2, 2, 2, then 3 minutes of work. Fraser's win here clinched his second consecutive title before the final event.

events.name: Fibonacci Final
events.description:
For time.

Men:
5 parallette handstand push-ups, 5 kettlebell deadlifts (2 x 203-lb kettlebells)
8 parallette handstand push-ups, 8 kettlebell deadlifts
13 parallette handstand push-ups, 13 kettlebell deadlifts
Then lunge 89 ft. with two 53-lb kettlebells held overhead.

Women:
3 parallette handstand push-ups, 5 kettlebell deadlifts (2 x 124-lb kettlebells)
5 parallette handstand push-ups, 8 kettlebell deadlifts
8 parallette handstand push-ups, 13 kettlebell deadlifts
Then lunge 89 ft. with two 35-lb kettlebells held overhead.

Time cap: 6 minutes.
events.notes: Rep counts (5, 8, 13) and the 89-ft. lunge follow the Fibonacci sequence; men and women used different handstand push-up rep schemes (5-8-13 vs 3-5-8) but the same 5-8-13 deadlift scheme. Strict parallette HSPU standards produced many no-reps; Logan Collins was the only man to finish under the 6-minute cap, with Fraser second at CAP+2 (two reps outstanding at the 6:00 cap per the official leaderboard). Kara Webb beat Tia-Clair Toomey in the event by 0.19 seconds but Toomey won the title by 2 points, the closest women's finish in Games history at the time.
